title: She didn't tell (Esther 2)
hook: Esther keeps her people and her kindred to herself at the palace

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vashti refused to be put on display, and lost her place. Your line was Vashti said no. Today, the empty seat is filled, by a young woman with a secret.

She has two names. The book introduces her as Hadassah, that is, Esther. She has neither father nor mother; her cousin Mordecai, the text says, took her for his own daughter. Then the king's officers gather young women from across the empire to the palace, and she is taken too. At that moment the book stops to tell us something she doesn't say.
screen: `HADASSAH, THAT IS, ESTHER.` → `RAISED BY HER COUSIN MORDECAI.` → `SOMETHING SHE DOESN'T SAY.`

segments.voice: She didn't tell. In the JPS 1917 translation: "Esther had not made known her people nor her kindred; for Mordecai had charged her that she should not tell it." She's in the house of the women, in the care of the king's chamberlain Hegai, and nobody there knows she's a Jew. The text doesn't say why Mordecai asked this. It lets you feel the danger without naming it. Then a small detail that's easy to miss. Every day Mordecai walks in front of the court of the women's house, to know how Esther did, and what would become of her. The text doesn't say he goes in. He walks past, every day, just to know how she is. When her turn comes to go to the king, she asks for nothing beyond what Hegai advises. The king loves her above all the women and sets the royal crown on her head. A great feast is held, Esther's feast. And then the book says it again, almost word for word: "Esther had not yet made known her kindred nor her people; as Mordecai had charged her." Now she's queen, and still she hasn't told. The repetition is the point. The crown didn't change the secret. In this story the silence reads less like shame than like waiting: one true thing held close until the day it's needed. The book doesn't say yet when that day will come. For now: not yet.
screen: `SHE HAD NOT MADE KNOWN HER PEOPLE.` · `MORDECAI WALKS PAST EVERY DAY.` · then, large: `CROWNED, AND STILL SHE HASN'T TOLD.` · then: `ONE TRUE THING, KEPT CLOSE.`

segments.voice: Ask yourself, gently, what part of who you are you keep quiet in certain rooms: a belief, a background, a language, a grief, a hope. You don't have to decide whether that's wise; just notice it, and think of one place or person where it would be safe to be seen. If you pray, bring what's hidden there too.
Hadassah. Esther's other name: she keeps her people and her kindred to herself, even after the crown. Today's word.
Your line: one true thing held close. The crown didn't change the secret. Day eight hundred sixty-five, done.

howItsDone: On Purim the scroll of Esther is chanted in synagogue, and the custom of dressing in costume is linked by some to the way Esther's identity stays hidden in the story.
